subsystems.name: Compliant body
subsystems.role: the structural material that bends instead of breaking, and sets the robot's range of motion.

subsystems.name: Actuation
subsystems.role: makes the body move without rigid joints.

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: lets the robot feel what it is touching, because it cannot see its own deformation easily.

subsystems.name: Fluid and power supply
subsystems.role: usually the bulkiest part, and often kept off the robot.

subsystems.name: Control
subsystems.role: commands soft structures whose exact shape is hard to model.

subsystems.name: Interface
subsystems.role: the part that touches the world or the patient.

buildSteps.title: Design the deformation
buildSteps.detail: Engineers decide how the body should bend, stretch or squeeze, then place internal channels, fibres and stiffening patches so pressurising a chamber produces that motion.

buildSteps.title: Make a mould
buildSteps.detail: A mould is 3D-printed or machined, often in several pieces, so the finished part can be pulled out without tearing.

buildSteps.title: Cast the elastomer
buildSteps.detail: Silicone or polyurethane is mixed, degassed to remove bubbles, poured into the mould and cured in an oven.

buildSteps.title: Add reinforcement and channels
buildSteps.detail: Fibre sheets limit expansion in chosen directions; soluble or printed cores create the hollow pneumatic channels, which are then cleared out.

buildSteps.title: Bond and embed sensors
buildSteps.detail: Layers are glued or co-cast together, and stretchable sensors, wiring or conductive tracks are embedded before the final cure.

buildSteps.title: Add fittings and valves
buildSteps.detail: Tubing, connectors and miniature valves are attached, and the robot is leak-tested at working pressure — typically a few hundred kilopascals.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and control
buildSteps.detail: A model or learned controller maps pressure, voltage or tendon tension to actual shape, and the behaviour is tuned against measurements.

buildSteps.title: Qualify it for use
buildSteps.detail: For medical or food-contact duties the device is cleaned, sterilised and tested for biocompatibility and fatigue over many thousands of cycles.

prerequisites.why: they provide the stretch, toughness and tear resistance the whole approach depends on.
compressed air is still the best actuator, but the supply hardware is heavy and hard to wear.
rigid wiring cracks when a soft body bends millions of times.
dielectric elastomers need kilovolts and degrade, so they are mostly lab devices.
controlling a body with infinite degrees of freedom is harder than controlling a jointed arm.

pathway.milestone: soft grippers handling delicate food and produce in factories, and flexible endoscopic tools in surgery
pathway.unlocks: automation of tasks that rigid metal hands crush or cannot reach.

pathway.milestone: wearable soft exosuits that assist walking and lifting in rehabilitation
pathway.unlocks: help for people with mobility loss, without a rigid frame.

pathway.milestone: soft implants such as conforming cardiac assist sleeves
pathway.unlocks: devices that move with living tissue instead of damaging it.

pathway.milestone: self-contained soft robots with on-board power, sensing and control
pathway.unlocks: field, inspection and home applications where a tether or compressor is impractical.
